Commentary.Commentary: 234 to win. That in-between score, which is neither too small, nor too commanding. The pitch has a green tinge, so the Indian seamers can exploit that. And then, the Indian spinners would have watched how Murphy bowled on this wicket - especially the ball to get Tilak Varma out - hmmm... they will fancy making it to the last 4. Join us back at 2 pm local (1200 GMT) for the run chase.

JP Duminy is having a chat with Todd Murphy. Murphy says that he is happy with his bowling performance and is happier with the Indian score as well. On the wicket, Todd says that there is a touch of green on the wicket and the seamers exploited that bounce, but he, as a spinner, just looked to bowl consistent lines and lengths. Admits that he tries to learn a lot by the way Nathan Lyon bowls. On going about chasing 234, Murphy says that it is usually difficult to defend scores at the backend of the innings, so if the batsmen can take it deep, get partnerships, he believes that they can chase it down.

Australia - well, they are always known to bowl well, aren't they? They did that here as well. But one thing has been plaguing them throughout this tournament - bowling at the death. 50 came in the last 5 today, 78 in the last 10. The momentum might have just shifted towards India. Willans and Sully were superb in their opening spell, not allowing much to the Indians and that resulted in frustration creeping through - eventually leading to wickets. Todd Murphy, who models his bowling on how Nathan Lyon bowls, was the most effective, taking 2 wickets and going for just 40. Tanveer Sangha though, Australia's sensation before this game, could not do much.

The defending champions had a small issue going into this game, which was the middle order. Given their clinical bowling display so far in the tournament, their middle order did not get much time in the middle. Australia gave them that test. The top order was removed cheaply, with the exception of Yashasvi Jaiswal and India were in trouble at 114/5 in the 31st over. But the lower middle order rallied around, getting meaningful stands, making sure that there was no collapse. Figure this out - 114 came in the first 31 - 119 came in the next 19. Of that, 61 came via the stand of Bishnoi and Ankolekar, that too, in just 59 balls. The latter went on to score an unbeaten 55, taking his side to a very good score.

That is more than a competitive total posted by India. At one stage, even 200 looked to be difficult to get but the Ankolekar-Bishnoi stand has given its side more than enough to bowl at. This is a ground where chasing is favoured but looking at the pitch, it does not look like a belter at all. Which means, bowlers will come into play. And India have plenty of those.
Very full ball on off, almost a yorker, Ankolekar has jammed it towards the cover region for a single. INDIA FINISH ON 233/9!

That looks nasty as Kelly has hurt himself in the process of taking a catch. Good length ball on middle, Ankolekar smashes this one down to long on. Kelly there runs to his right and dives forward trying to take the catch but he fails to do so. Instead, it looks like he has injured his shoulder. He gets up and throws the ball towards the non-striker's end but in the meantime the batters take two runs. Kelly is in visible pain here.

OUT! RUN OUT! Tyagi sacrifices his wicket for his side! Length ball on middle and leg, Atharva slaps another one down to long on. Kelly there collects and throws the ball towards the non-striker's end. Tyagi knows he has to go for the second even if it was not there because that would mean Ankolekar would be on strike. He tries to reach there but the bails are whipped off and he is not even in the frame. Tyagi departs, but more importantly, Ankolekar will face the next ball.

SIX! Super shot by Atharva Ankolekar and what a way to get to your first half ton. Back of a length ball outside off, Ankolekar has slapped this one over the long on fence for a biggie. He has taken India to a very decent total here with his very good knock under pressure. Now, he will look to score as much as he can off the last 3 deliveries.
Length ball way outside off, Atharva goes for a wild slash but misses.
Full ball on middle, Tyagi has worked this towards mid-wicket for a single.
FOUR! Very nicely played! Very full outside off, Atharva uses the pace of the ball and just guides it away from short third man for a boundary.
On the pads, Atharva glances it to the leg side for another couple.

Fuller on middle, Ankolekar whips it wide of long on and gets a couple. He was running on the wicket and hence he has been warned for running onto the danger area. Also, they have ran one short, so they will get just a single.
Kartik Tyagi walks out now.

OUT! Caught! Good catch from the skipper. Not the wicket of Atharva but it is Sushant who departs. More importantly for Australia it's a dot ball. Fuller ball around the pads, Mishra tries to flick it over but ends up getting a leading edge which flies behind cover. Mackenzie Harvey runs behind and takes a very good catch as running behind and taking a catch is one of the most toughest things to do. They look easy on the television but it is not as easy as they seem.
On the pads, Ankolekar turns it to the on side for a single.

FOUR! Innovative and Atharva's bold move reaps the reward. Full outside off, Atharva gets in a position to paddle and hits it over the keeper's head. You cannot keep a man in there and he gets a boundary. These are crucial runs for India.
WIDE! Willans misses his line completely and sprays one well down the leg side. Atharva lets it be and it has been wided.
FOUR! Good start for Mishra as he cuts this length ball outside off through point and the ball races away into the fence. Off the mark in style.
The new man in is Sushant Mishra.

OUT! RUN OUT! Brilliant fielding from Sam Fanning and the stand that has taken India to a respectable total has now been broken. Good length ball on middle and leg, Bishnoi works it behind square and looks for two. They complete the first and Bishnoi sets off for the second. Fanning at deep backward square leg collects the ball and sends a strong throw towards the keeper's end. Rowe there collects the ball and whips the bails off as Bishnoi puts in the dive. The umpire immediately refers it upstairs. Replays roll in to show that Bishnoi is well short and he has to depart. The 60-run stand has been broken and Australia again stealing the momentum away from India.
Run out appeal taken upstairs. Bishnoi is the man in question. Is the dive enough to save Bishnoi? Let's see what the replay has to say.
The batsman has top edged that one. They pick up a single.
On the pads of Ankolekar, he works this one behind the fielder at square leg for a couple.

NOT OUT! A very full ball outside off, Ankolekar looks to jam it out and does so towards the man at point. The fielder there catches the ball and appeals for a catch. The umpire refers this one upstairs to double-check. Replays roll in to show that the ball hit the bat, then the ground and then into the hands of the fielder.
Is it a bump ball or is it a catch? The Australians feel its a catch. The soft signal is NOT OUT! So the third umpire will need concrete evidence to overturn that.
FOUR! Beautiful shot by Ankolekar! Full ball on off, Ankolekar leans and has creamed this one through the cover region for a boundary.

That is unlucky for the fielder. Full ball on middle and off, flicked towards the square leg region. The batters take a single. The throw comes in from there and it hits the stumps at the striker's end which allows the batters to take two.
Ankolekar has played it towards mid-wicket. They pick up a single.
Full ball on the pads, Bishnoi again flicks this one towards mid-wicket for a single. 50-run stand up between these two and it has been pivotal for India.
Good wrist work by Ankolekar as he flicks this one towards mid-wicket for a single.
Another full ball on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
Full ball on the pads, worked towards the leg side for a single.
This time Ankolekar connects and guides it down to third man for a single.
Another delivery outside off, Ankolekar looks to play at it but misses.
FOUR! Good shot! Good length ball outside off, Ankolekar does well to cut this one past the man at point and the ball goes into the fence.
On the pads of Bishnoi, he flicks this one towards mid-wicket and the batters take a single.
Back of a length ball on off, extra bounce on it, Bishnoi looks to play at this one but the ball whizzes past him.
Length ball outside off, Ankolekar guides it down to third man for a single.
Connor Sully is back. 7-1-26-1, his numbers so far.
Floated outside off, Bishnoi looks to play at it but misses.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! A delivery that is dragged back by Sangha, Bishnoi punches this off the back foot through the cover region for a boundary.
Floated delivery on middle and off, Ankolekar plays this one towards the man at mid-wicket region for a single.
Loopy delivery on middle, worked towards the man at wide long on for a single.
Floated on off, pushed towards the cover region.
Wide! Down the leg side, Bishnoi does not fiddle with it.
On the pads, flicked towards the mid-wicket region for a single.
Ankolekar punches this one down to long on for a single.
Floated on off, pushed down to long off for a single.
Floated outside off, Bishnoi goes for the sweep shot but misses.
Floated delivery on middle, worked towards the leg side for a single.
Floated delivery outside off, Bishnoi looks to play at it but misses. The ball ricochets of the keeper's hand towards the leg side and the batters take a bye.
Oliver Davies is back. Just a run so far from his solitary over.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball.
Full and around middle, watchfully blocked out.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a run.
Full toss, on middle and leg, flicked to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Around middle, pushed back towards Sangha again.
Full and around middle, driven straight back to the bowler.
Shorter outside off, Ankolekar runs it down to third man and get a single.
Outside off, left alone.
Flighted on off, Bishnoi pushes it towards cover for a single.
On the pads, Bishnoi glances it wide of fine leg and gets a couple.

Ankolekar wanted two but Bishnoi was not too keen. A little bit of confusion there. On the pads, Ankolekar flicks it towards fine leg and dashes the first one. He comes out for the second but Bishnoi does not see him. He then sees him and comes out as the fielder sends in the throw but by then Atharva sends him back.

EDGED AND FOUR! Very good ball from Kelly, he deserved a wicket off that ball. If first slip would have been there then it would have been curtains for Atharva. Full outside off, Ankolekar goes for the drive but gets a thick outside edge. Rowe dives to his left but the ball is far away from him and goes to the fence.
Tossed up outside off, Bishnoi slams it wide of sweeper cover for a couple.
Outside off, Bishnoi leaves it alone.
Flighted on the stumps, Atharva blocks it.
Loopy full toss on middle, Ankolekar squeezes it to long on for one.
Full toss outside off, Ankolekar cannot get under it and hits it towards deep mid-wicket for a run.
Floated outside off, Atharva hits it hard but there is a man at long on so just one.
Sangha is back. 8-1-25-1, his figures so far.
Powerplay 3 is underway! A maximum of 5 fielders can now be placed outside the circle until the end of the innings.
On the pads, Bishnoi turns it behind square on the leg side. He calls for two straightaway and gets it with ease. Good call and good running from the Indian pair. They need a lot more of these.
Length ball outside off, Bishnoi leaves it alone.
Full on off, Bishnoi looks to defend but even he gets a thick inside edge which goes wide of deep mid-wicket for a couple.
Full on middle, Atharva checks his straight drive. The ball takes the outside edge and goes towards backward point for a single.
Good length delivery outside off, Ankolekar looks to defend but misses.
Very good bowling from Kelly. Yorker outside off, Atharva looks to defend but misses.
On the pads again, defended towards the leg side.

SIX! Bishnoi would have had his heart in his mouth for a moment there but it has cleared the fence. Tossed up on middle, Bishnoi gets down on one knee and goes for the slog. He connects and the ball just about clears Kelly at deep mid-wicket for a maximum. 150 up for India with this shot.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
Floated on off now, pushed back towards the bowler.
Floated on middle and leg, worked towards the leg side.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Ravi Bishnoi is the new man in.

OUT! Siddhesh holes out! Kelly who was hit for two boundaries in the over by Veer has the last laugh. Good length delivery around off, Siddhesh getting greedy for more runs even after getting 8 off the over goes for the big pull. He does not manage to time it as the ball comes quicker off the surface. Veer ends up getting a top edge which flies straight towards third man. Todd Murphy there keeps his eyes on the ball and takes an easy catch. Once again when it looks like India are on course to build something Australia break those dreams.
Play and a miss! Good length ball outside off, Veer looks to defend but misses.
FOUR! Cut away this time. Second boundary off the over. Length ball outside off, Siddhesh gets on his back foot and cuts it like a knife going through butter towards point for a boundary.
Good comeback from Kelly. He hits the deck hard outside off, the ball shoots up off the surface. Veer looks to defend but misses.
FOUR! Pulled away with disdain. Back of a length ball around off, Siddhesh gets on his back foot and whacks his pull through mid-wicket for a boundary.
Good length ball outside off, Veer lets it carry to the keeper.
Kelly is back! 23/1 from his 7.
Shorter on off, Ankolekar punches it to mid off and gets through the over.
The batsman has driven that ball straight back.
Slower through the air on off, Atharva looks to defend but gets a thick outside edge which sees the ball go towards third man for a couple.
Now strokes it to long off for an easy single.
Tossed up on off, Veer punches it to cover.
Flighted outside off, Siddhesh leaves it alone.
Quicker one outside off, Ankolekar pushes it to cover. Good over from Davies, just a single off it.
Flights one on the stumps, Ankolekar defends it.
On the pads, Ankolekar flicks it to the on side.
Flighted on the stumps, Ankolekar blocks it.
Floated on middle and leg, Atharva strokes it to mid on.
Flatter on the pads, Veer tucks it to the on side for a single.
Oliver Davies is on now.
Outside off, left alone by Ankolekar. 15 overs to go from here. Can India get to the 220-run mark?
Good length delivery on off, Veer looks to defend but the ball goes off the outside edge through the gully region for a single.
Willans bowls it down the leg side, Veer helps it fine down the leg side. Sangha there misfields and allows the batters to take two. So just the two runs off the Free Hit.
FREE HIT TIME!!!
No ball! Another huge no ball by Willans as he has overstepped! Full ball on the pads, tickled down to fine leg for a single.
Now Veer opens the face of the bat and guides it down to third man for a single.
Length ball outside off, angled down to third man for a single.
Good start right after the Drinks break! Willans bowls a length ball just around the off pole line and gets it to nip away from the batter. Ankolekar looks to defend but gets completely squared up.

Drinks Break! Australia are well and truly on top of the game. They have sent half the Indian boys back in the pavilion and are into the untested lower middle order. They have bowled well so far and will look to restrict India under 200. India, on the other hand, need to get close to the 250 mark here. The onus will be on the current pair of Siddhesh Veer and Atharva Ankolekar to take them as close to that mark as possible.
Murphy drags his length back, Veer goes back and blocks this one out.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated on middle and off, Veer looks to defend but the ball goes off the inside edge onto the pads.
Siddhesh prods forward and defends this ball back towards Murphy.
Flatter delivery near the boots, played towards the mid on fielder.
Floated on middle, the batsman has driven it straight down the ground.
FIVE WIDES! Flatter delivery down the leg side, Veer looks to go for the sweep but misses and so does the keeper. The ball races to the fine leg fence.
Ohh! Extra bounce! Back of a length ball on off, it pitches and takes off. Ankolekar has left that one alone.
Edged but safe! Good length ball outside off, Ankolekar looks to have a poke at it but the ball goes off the outside edge and falls just short of the man at first slip.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended back towards the bowler.
Another length ball just outside off, played towards the man at point.
Length ball on off, punched off the back foot towards cover for a single.
Length ball on off, played towards the man at point.
Matthew Willans, the tall pacer, is back on. 6-1-13-0, his figures so far.
Short and outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
Outside off, punched off the back foot towards cover.
Around off, solidly blocked out.
FOUR! VIOLENCE! He has hit that really hard. Full on middle, Veer powers this past the bowler through mid on. Long on gets across to his right but cannot get there!
Full and around off, well defended.
Full and around middle, Veer flicks it through mid-wicket where the fielder dives to his left to stop the ball.
Atharva Ankolekar is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT! Dhruv Jurel runs out of patience and he has thrown his wicket away. A floated and tempting delivery on middle and off, Jurel looks to come down the ground and hoick this one down over the leg side. But he is nowhere near the pitch of the ball and the drift and loop from Murphy ensure that the batsman is early into the shot. He gets a top edge on it and the ball goes up towards the keeper. Patrick Rowe there takes an easy catch and Dhruv Jurel makes his way back to the pavilion after a promising start.
Loopy delivery on middle and off, pushed down to the man at mid off.
Jurel rocks back and defends this shortish ball off the back foot.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, defended.
On the pads, defended towards the leg side.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Jurel opens the face of his bat and plays this one down to third man for a couple.
Todd Murphy is back on.
Sangha drags his length back. Veer rocks back and defends.
On the pads, tucked towards the man at mid-wicket.
FOUR! Some runs for the Indians! Floated delivery on the middle and leg pole line, Veer gets down on one knee and paddles it fine down the leg side for a boundary.
Tossed up delivery on off, pushed towards long off and the batters take a single.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, defended towards the off side.
Floated delivery outside off, Jurel drives this one towards the man at cover.
Outside off, Veer leaves it alone to get through the over.
On the pads of Jurel, he works this one towards the leg side and gets a single.
Bouncer now from Sully, Jurel does well to duck under it.
Full and on off, Jurel drives it superbly towards the cover region but the man there dives and makes a superb shot.
Beauty by Sully! He bowls a full delivery on off, Jurel looks to have a poke at this one but the ball holds its line and beats the outside edge of Jurel's bat.
Full delivery on middle and off, defended by Jurel.
Another ball which is shortish in length, Jurel cuts and this one towards point for a single.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Sangha drags his length back and Siddhesh pulls this one towards square leg for a single.
Loopy delivery on off and Jurel has driven it towards cover for a single.
Floated outside off, it pitches and turns away. Jurel makes the leave.
Floated on middle and off, played back towards the bowler.
Bouncer on off, left alone by Siddhesh to get through the over.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Full delivery on middle and off, Veer plays this one towards mid off. Jurel wants the run but is sent back by Veer just in time with the Aussie fielders closing in.
Length delivery outside off, left alone.
Length ball on middle and leg, Veer rocks back and pulls but straight to the man at square leg.
Good length ball on the off pole line, defended back towards the bowler. The batters take a single as the man from mid on runs to his left and cuts it off.

What an over from Sangha! Champion comeback from him. He went for 12 in his first over but he has come back here and bowled a maiden including getting rid of the big fish, Yashasvi Jaiswal. Flatter on off, Siddhesh defends it to get through the over.
Around off, Veer blocks it.
Once again it is short from Sangha and Siddhesh punches it off his back foot.
Short outside off, Veer gets on his back foot and plays it to point.
Shorter on off, Veer blocks it off his back foot.
Siddhesh Veer walks out to bat now.

OUT! BOWLED! Massive wicket for Australia as India's young run machine goes back to the pavillion. The glue of the Indian innings so far has to depart. After going for 12 in his first over, Sangha has come back and given his side the biggest wicket of the game. Short on middle and leg, Jasiwal gets on his back foot and looks to go for a big smash on the leg side. He misses as the ball turns in a bit more than he anticipated and the ball hits his thigh and goes right between his legs to disturb the stumps. 11th wicket for Sangha in this tournament and every time Australia needs a wicket, the leg spinner delivers. India into uncharted territory here as their untested middle order will have to deliver on the big stage now.
Short outside off, Jaiswal cuts it towards point and keeps the strike.
Flights one on off, Yashasvi blocks it.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Short around off, Jaiswal cuts it towards point and gets a couple.
Tossed up outside off, Jaiswal leaves it alone.
Flighted on off, Jaiswal defends it with a straight bat.
On the stumps, Jurel blocks it. Expensive start for Sangha, 12 from his first. Much-needed big over for India.
Once again short but closer to the off pole. Jaiswal runs it down to third man for a single.
FOUR! Now a boundary! WOW! This guy is a serious talent. Short and wide outside off, Jaiswal now gets on his back foot and punches it through cover-point for a boundary.

SIX! That was six the moment it left the bat. Jaiswal brings his fifty up in style. Pressure game and the talented Yashasvi is leading his side from the front. We saw a couple of those against New Zealand as well. Flighted delivery outside off, Yashasvi gets on his knee and smokes his slog sweep well over the mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Shorter on middle and leg, Jurel punches it towards long on for a single.
Floated leg spinner on middle, Jurel gets on his front foot and defends it.
Change in bowling as Tanveer Sangha is brought into the attack for the first time today.
This time Jurel flicks it in the gap at mid-wicket and gets a single.
On the pads, flicked towards the man at mid-wicket again.
Tossed up on middle, worked towards the leg side.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.

Woah! Opportunity missed maybe! Floated delivery down the leg side, Jurel comes down the track and looks to heave but misses. The ball goes off his pads down to fine leg and the batters take two leg byes. Had the keeper collected it, Jurel would have been out stumped for sure!
Floated just outside the off pole line, played uppishly towards the man at mid-wicket.
Good length ball on middle and leg, defended back towards the bowler.
Full ball on middle and off, driven towards the man at mid on.
This time a good length ball outside off, Jaiswal shoulders arms.
Length ball on the pads, worked towards the leg side again.
FOUR! Great shot! Full ball on the pads, Jaiswal flicks this one through the mid-wicket region and bags a boundary. No need for any fielders to move.
Length ball just around off, left alone.
Floated on off, pushed towards sweeper cover for a single.
Another one which is dragged back by Murphy, Jaiswal drives it through the covers for another couple.
Shortish ball on off, Jaiswal rocks back and cuts this one towards deep point for a couple.
Floated outside off, it spins away. Left alone.
Jaiswal looks to poke at this floated delivery on off but edges this one.
Shortish ball on off, played towards the man at point.

Jurel was looking for a quick run but cannot get it. Good length ball on the pads, Jurel tucks it to the leg side and looks for a quick single. Jaiswal sends his partner back and it is a good call as the fielder was quick to get to the ball.
Outside off on a length, Jurel punches it to cover.
Wide outside off, Jurel drives it but cannot go past point.
Length delivery around off, Jurel defends it with a dead bat.
Good length ball outside off, Jurel plays it to cover.
On the pads, Jaiswal turns it to fine leg for a run.
On the stumps, Dhruv blocks it. 5 off the over.
Murphy flights one on off, Yashasvi strokes it through covers for a run.
Flighted around the pads, Jaiswal sweeps it through square leg. Kelly at deep mid-wicket does well to chase it and stop it before the ropes. Two taken.
Flighted on the stumps, YJ calmly defends it.
Tossed up around off, Dhruv strokes it to long on for a run.
Flighted outside off, Jaiswal drives it towards long off for a single.
Todd Murphy is back on. 2-0-10-1, his figures so far.
Another good stroke but straight to the fielder. Full around off, Jurel drives it very nicely but straight to cover.
Full on off, Jurel pushes it to cover.
Outside off, Jaiswal cuts it wide of point for a run.

Under edge and a couple. Good length ball outside off, Yashasvi looks to cut but it goes off the bottom half of his bat. The ball bounces just in front of Patrick Rowe, the keeper. He fails to stop it and the ball deflects off him towards third man for a couple.
Outside off, left alone.
Length ball outside off, Jaiswal guides it wide of third man for a couple.
WIDE! Short ball on the leg side, it is high as well so the umpire stretches his arms and signals it as wide.
Uppish and FOUR! Fuller on middle, Jurel chips his flick wide of mid-wicket and gets his first boundary of the game. There were shouts of catch it but the fielder had no chance.
The physio is out in the middle. He is conducting the mandatory concussion check on Dhruv Jurel.

FOUR LEG BYES! Off the helmet! Short ball on middle and leg, Jurel initially looks to duck under it so he sits. But then he changes his mind and goes for the pull but he misses and the ball clips his helmet and goes to the fine leg fence.
Another one away from the off pole and Dhruv shoulders arms to it.
Length ball outside off, Jurel leaves it alone.

Huge appeal but the umpire turns it down. Good length delivery pitching around off and coming back in. Jurel lunges forward and looks to play on the up but misses. The ball hits him high on his back leg. The Australian players go up in appeal but the umpire after a brief thought shakes his head.
Good length delivery outside off, Jurel leaves it alone.
Matthew Kelly is back into the attack. 4-0-14-1, his figures so far.

Edged and a single. Full outside off, even this one comes back in. Jurel looks to drive but gets a thick inside edge which goes towards fine leg for a single. Not the most convincing way to get off the mark but he will take it.

Another good delivery from Sully. It is pacy and on a length on middle and leg. It comes back in. Jurel looks to defend but misses and the ball hits him high on the pads. There is stifled appeal but nothing from the umpire.
Short ball outside off, Jurel sways away from it.
Good length ball on off, Jurel starts his innings with a calm defense.

DRINKS! India on the back foot! Now that is a thing that we have not witnessed in a long time. The openers started strongly for India but the Australian bowlers have kept working hard and have got their rewards. It is time for the Indian middle order to step up now and with Yashasvi Jaiswal still at the crease, India can still make a very good comeback. Dhruv Jurel has walked in now to replace his skipper.

OUT! BOWLED! India under the pump as their skipper is heading back to the pavillion. Right through the gate of bat and pad. Sully comes back and delivers straightaway. Sully steams in and bowls a full ball on off, it nips back in. Garg tries to play a drive but leaves a huge gap between the bat and pad. The gap is so big that a train could go through there. He misreads the swing and the ball goes right between that gap to disturb the stumps. India succumbing under pressure and now the onus will be on the untested middle order to take them out of troubled waters. Australia all over India here.
Good length delivery around off, Jaiswal dabs it towards point for a run.
Connor Sully is back on.
Outside off, floated delivery, played towards point. 4 runs come off the over.
Murphy drags his length back and Garg rocks back and defends.
Tossed up delivery outside off, Jaiswal rocks back and runs it down to third man. The fielder gives it a chase and does well as he keeps it down to three.
On the pads, worked towards square leg and the batters take a single.
Tossed up delivery on middle and off, Garg looks to defend but the ball comes off the inside edge and hits Garg onto the pads.
Floated on middle and off, worked towards the leg side.
Jaiswal showing his patience as he leaves another delivery which is outside off.
Another one which is outside off, Jaiswal does not fiddle with it.
Outside off, Jaiswal leaves this one alone.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full ball on middle and off, driven towards the man at wide mid off superbly.
This time Kelly corrects his line a bit and Jaiswal yet again shoulders arms.
Wide! Way outside off, Jaiswal does not go chasing after it.
FOUR! A full toss outside off, Garg comes forward and drives this one through the cover region for a boundary and a wonderful way to get off the mark.
India in a bit of a bother here and the skipper, Priyam Garg walks out to bat.

OUT! CAUGHT! Tilak Varma departs and Australia making inroads now! A floated delivery just around the off pole line, it pitches and straightens. There is extra bounce on it as well. Varma looks to prod forward and defend but the ball goes off the splice of the bat high towards first slip where Mackenzie jumps high and takes a very good catch right above his head. Australia making life difficult for India right now!
On the pads, flicked towards the mid-wicket region for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Tossed up outside off, played towards the man at point.
Floated on off, pushed down to long off and the batters take a single.
Time for spin now. Australia have had majority success in this tournament because of spin and Todd Murphy is into the attack.
Full ball on middle and off, driven towards the man at long off and the batters take a single.
Another one outside off, played towards the point region for a single.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Full ball on off, pushed towards the man at cover.
Length ball around off, Jaiswal again looks to have a poke at it but misses.

EDGED AND FOUR! That one almost carried to the man at first slip. Good length ball on middle and off, angling away. Jaiswal looks to have a poke at it but the ball goes off the outside edge through the gap at first slip and the keeper. The fielder dives to his right but misses and the ball races into the third man fence.
Good length ball on middle and off, defended off the front foot and into the ground.
On off, played towards the point region.

Good length ball on the off pole line, angling into Varma. He looks to make the leave but is hit on the pads outside the leg pole line so no appeal from the bowler but the slip cordon was interested. Nothing from the umpire.
Fuller ball on off, Varma looks to drive this towards the off side but the ball moves and misses his bat.
Another length ball around off, Varma thinks about playing at it but takes his bat away at the last moment.
Length ball on off, Jaiswal plays it towards point and changes ends.
Powerplay 2 is underway! A maximum of 4 fielders can now be placed outside the circle till the 40th over.

Full on middle and off, Tilak defends it with a dead bat to start his innings. End of a superb over from Kelly. Just a single and a wicket off the over to end Powerplay 1! India 35/1 in the first phase of the innings.
Tilak Varma is the new man in.

OUT! Caught! Beautiful line and length from Kelly and it has reaped its reward. Kelly hits the deck hard on the channel. It is in the corridor of uncertainty. To add to the wonders of this delivery Kelly even manages to generate extra bounce making this almost unplayable. Saxena hops and looks to defend but that extra bounce and little away movement sees it kisses the outside edge of Divyaansh's bat and go straight into the gloves of Patrick Rowe. A well-deserved wicket for the Aussies as they have been very good with their lines and lengths and now they have something to show for all the pressure they have built.
Back of a length around off, Saxena dabs it towards backward point.
Good shot but straight to the fielder. Full on middle and off, Saxena lunges forward and drives it right off the middle but straight to the man at cover.
Better from Kelly. Hits the deck hard around off, Saxena leaves it alone.
WIDE! Too wide from the off stump. On the wrong end of the tramline. Wided by the umpire.
On the hips, Saxena works it towards the leg side.
Full and outside off, asking YJ to drive but he is not going to fall in this trap.
Length ball outside off, once again Yashasvi leaves it alone.
Back of a length around off, Jaiswal taps it towards point.
Bouncer! Too high and also down the leg side. Jasiwal gets inside the line of it and leaves it. Wided by the umpire.
Good length ball away from the off stump, Yashasvi leaves it alone.
Good ball! Fuller just outside off, it zips away. Jaiswal leaves it alone.
Good length delivery outside off, there was width for Jaiswal to have a go but he shows maturity and leaves it alone. So far the pair of Jaiswal and Saxena is happy to see off Willans.
Length delivery on middle and off, swinging away from Saxena. He looks to defend but the ball moves and misses his blade.
FOUR! Good shot but bad ball! On the pads of Saxena, he flicks this one through the mid-wicket region for a boundary. Good start for the Indians so far.
Way outside the off pole line, Saxena leaves this one alone.
Full ball on off, Saxena drives this one through the cover region. The fielder there dives and makes a half stop. The batters take two runs by the time the fielder mops it up.
Similar delivery, Saxena again looks to punch through the cover region but again the man there dives and stops it.
Full ball on off to start with by Saxena, he plays a superb cover drive but straight to the man.
First bowling change of the game as Conor Kelly is into the attack.
FOUR! Caressed! Beautiful drive by Jaiswal! Full ball on off, driven through the cover region and no one can stop that one as the ball races away to the fence.
Good length ball on the off pole line, angling in. Jaiswal looks to defend but is late in bringing his bat down and is rapped on the pads outside the leg pole line.
Full ball on middle and off, pushed towards the man at mid off.
Length ball outside off, Saxena plays this one towards the man at deep point and takes a single.
Outside off, left alone by Saxena.
FOUR! This time Saxena with a wonderful shot! Length ball outside off again, Saxena now cuts through the point region and beats the man in the deep.
FOUR! Wonderful stroke by Jaiswal! Back of a length ball on off, Jaiswal goes back and cut this one through the point region for a boundary.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
Way wide outside off, Jaiswal leaves this one alone.
Bouncer on middle and off, Jaiswal ducks under it.
Another one on middle and off, played towards the point region and the batters take a single.
Length ball on off, played towards the man at point.
Another delivery which is way outside off, Jaiswal leaves it alone.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Free hit and Jaiswal looks to shuffle and loft this over the leg side but he fails to connect as Willans bowls a slower delivery and it hits Jaiswal on the pads.
No ball! Overstepping by a big margin! Willans has bowled this one way outside off and Jaiswal has left that one alone too.
Outside off, pitching and moving further away. Willans looking to tempt Jaiswal into the drive but Yashasvi is patient and leaves it alone.
Another one which is way wide outside off, Jaiswal is not bothered at all and leaves it alone.
Length ball way outside off, Willans leaves that alone.

Third time in a row that Sully has beaten Saxena and the last ball is a real beauty from him. Good length delivery starting on off, it zips away from Divyaansh. He looks to drive it on the up and misses. Very good comeback from Connor, after going for 11 in his first he has come up and bowled a very good maiden.
Good bowling from Connor Sully. He pitches it up outside off, tempting Saxena to go for the drive. He falls in the trap and goes for it but misses.
Swing and a miss from Saxena. Full and wide outside off, Divyaansh throws his bat at it but only connects with thin air. Trying to release some pressure with that shot.
Back of a length around the body, Divyaansh goes on his back foot and blocks it. Much better over so far from Sully.
Fuller on middle, Saxena defends it with a straight bat.
Length ball on middle, Divyaansh hops and defends it towards cover-point.
On the fourth stump line, Jaiswal calmly shoulders arms to this one.
Fuller on off, Jaiswal pushes it to cover.
Outside off, Yashasvi does not go chasing after it.
Willans offers width this time outside off, Saxena cuts it wide of point and gets a single. First run off Willans' bowling.
Beautiful delivery! Willans bowls a beautiful line, on the channel on off. It shapes away off the deck. Saxena looks to defend but gets beaten.
Good length delivery outside off, Saxena leaves it alone.

SIX! What a shot! He has just picked that up over the square leg fence. Sully is guilty of bowling on Jaiswal's pad. Yashasvi just picks it up from there and sends it sailing over the fence. Expensive start for Sully, 11 off his first.
Outside off, Yashasvi leaves it alone.
Yorker wide outside off. Jaiswal looks to dab but misses.
Good fielding from Fanning, saves runs for his side. Around the pads, Jaiswal flicks it right off the meat but Fanning at short mid-wicket dives to his left and saves a certain boundary.

FOUR! Beautiful shot! A shot of a batsman with real class. His patience has paid off. He has been calm to start but now he gets an overpitched delivery on off and middle. Yashavi gets on his front foot and drives it straight down the ground to score the first boundary of the game.
Sully starts with a fuller delivery on middle on leg and middle, Saxena flicks it towards mid-wicket and gets off the mark. First run of the day.
Connor Sully to partner Willans from the other end.

Superb start for Australia and Willans. It is a maiden to start the game. Good length delivery around off, Jaiswal defends it off his back foot towards point and gets through the first over without scoring any run.
Length ball outside off, Willans bowls it with good seam position. The ball keeps going further away and Jaiswal is not interested in that so he lets it go.
Length delivery on middle and off, Jaiswal hops and defends it off his back foot. It comes off the lower half of his bat and goes onto hit his pad.
Good length delivery on off, it shapes away. Jaiswal gets on his back foot and defends it from the middle of his willow.
Willans goes full on off, Jaiswal gets bat on ball for the first time and pushes it to mid off from the middle of the bat.
Willans is right on the money first up. A little bit of movement for the tall left-arm seamer. It starts around off and moves away just a bit. Yashasvi is aware of his off pole and leaves it alone.

Done and dusted with the national anthems and we are all set for the action to begin. The Australian team make their way out to the middle along with the Indian openers, Yashasvi Jaiswal and Divyaansh Saxena. Matthew Willans to start off the proceedings with the ball. Here we go!
Both sets of players walk out for their respective national anthems. We are not far away from the start of the action. First up it will be Australia's followed by India's.
Indian skipper, Priyam Garg, says he is happy to bat first. Says that this is another challenge for his side and they are looking forward to it. Informs that there are no changes to the side.

Australian skipper, Mackenzie Harvey says they are bowling first as he thinks there will be something for the bowlers on the pitch and hopes his bowlers can pick early wickets and expose the Indian middle order. Informs there are two changes in his side as Matthew Willians and Corey Kelly come in for Liam Scott and Bradley Simpson. Says he is not concerned about the batting issue as he knows they have depth in the side and expects them to fire soon.

Pitch Report - Dominic Cork and JP Duminy are the pitch analysts for the day. Says the ball will fly as we are well above sea levels so expects batsmen to enjoy it. JP Duminy agrees that it will be a run fest and tells there is live grass on the pitch and it will come onto play. Tells there can be a little moisture in the first hour.

India U19 (Unchanged Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal, Divyaansh Saxena, Tilak Varma, Priyam Garg (C), Dhruv Jurel(WK), Siddhesh Veer, Atharva Ankolekar, Ravi Bishnoi, Sushant Mishra, Kartik Tyagi and Akash Singh.

Australia U19 (Playing XI) - Sam Fanning, Jake Fraser-McGurk, Mackenzie Harvey (C), Lachlan Hearne, Oliver Davies, Patrick Rowe (WK), Corey Kelly, Connor Sully, Tanveer Sangha, Todd Murphy, Matthew Willans.
Toss - Up goes the coin and it lands in the favour of Australia. They have opted to field.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the U-19 World Cup quarterfinal between India and Australia. The Boys in Blue have been one of the strongest sides and have showed why they are the favourites to win the tournament heading into this fixture. Australia, on the other hand, managed to get here courtesy of a thrilling win against England. The Aussies will look to upset the tournament favourites in their toughest challenge yet. Can the young Australians stun the Indians or will the defending champions continue their dominance?
